piece: Reconcile the two soul ledgers that disagree by 53% — population-posts.json's cached roll-up against the statblocks that actually pay. corpus/90-verdicts/wave1/W1-SOULS-r3.md §2.1 and §9 (GAP-W1-souls-world-copy-of-the-values-is-53pc-stale) is the spec.
next_step: Nothing outstanding for this piece. A critic should grade it. The one open decision is handed to the orchestrator under player_facing_totals_that_moved below.
ownership_note: game/data/world/population-posts.json is generated by tools/world/build-population.mjs, which W1-POPULATION owns and which is `complete`. I did not modify the generator — I re-ran it, which is the remedy W1-SOULS-r3 §9 prescribes. tools/check-data.mjs and tools/gen-index.mjs were unclaimed by any live piece. The three annotations under corpus/90-verdicts/ and orchestration/status/ belong to pieces that are all `complete` and none of which appear in `node tools/ownership.mjs`; each is a single ADDITIVE, dated, attributed erratum that alters nothing above it, and the two JSON files were edited as text and re-parsed so a neighbour's file gained two lines rather than a 200-line re-encoding diff.
contention: node tools/contention.mjs --gate read WAIT at start (5 instances, 5.11/core). Every ledger arm is offline JSON arithmetic and needed no browser, so that work was done first, as RULES 21 asks. Re-gated GO (2 instances, 3.50/core) before the CONSUMPTION leg; one browser launched and kept for the whole of it. No wall-clock or millisecond figure appears anywhere in this piece — every number is a soul count, a body count, a level, a row count or a percentage.

q1_which_ledger_is_the_truth.how_confirmed_by_reading: game/src/sim/souls.js:320 — on the alive->dead transition SoulsSystem.step() computes awardFor(this.d[e.id], awardHour) and adds .souls to sim.progression.soulsHeld. `this.d` IS Engine.data.enemies (engine.js:498), which is game/data/combat/enemies/*.json. It is the only producer of souls in the build (the r3 verdict §7 enumerates all five writers of soulsHeld). It never opens population-posts.json. Conversely, a grep for readers of the cached field across game/src finds exactly ONE — game/src/world/population.js:294, `souls_total: this.posts.reduce((a,p) => a + (p.souls||0), 0)`, inside report(), whose own comment says 'What a probe reads. Never used by the simulation.'
q1_which_ledger_is_the_truth.how_confirmed_by_running: tools/souls-consumption-ledger.mjs arm E. A real population post materialised by the shipping streamer (teleport to it, let PopulationSystem.step() bring it on), its cached `souls` set to 3x+7 of its real worth (73 against 22), its bodies killed through the shipping kill path. The player was paid 22. The cache was lying and the money followed the statblocks.
q1_which_ledger_is_the_truth.how_confirmed_by_provenance: population-posts.json last written at e54a18a, 2026-08-07 18:50. The seven statblocks W1-SOULS round 3 re-derived were written at 0c8acfa 22:36 and e97347f 00:50 — after it. The cache is the older document, not a competing opinion.

The souls-specific check names the row.

player_facing_totals_that_moved.reasoning: This piece re-tuned nothing. Level 3 is what the shipped statblocks and the shipped levels.json curve have paid since e97347f; level 5 was only ever the cache saying so, and no player has ever been paid it. Publishing 3 corrects a lie rather than making a change. But if the DESIGN wants the Stormhold->Lilmoth crossing to buy level 5, the lever is the souls economy (RI-PRG06 / tools/progression/derive-soul-values.mjs) or the population density (RI-WLD02 / game/data/world/population.json) — not this reconciliation, and a critic graded the economy an hour ago.

not_done: I did not re-tune the economy, the curve or the level ladder. Out of scope by the brief and a critic graded them an hour ago.

I did not close the other four findings in W1-SOULS-r3 §10 — the oracle's breadth (343 routes = 14 behaviour vectors over one statblock at one hour), giving invariant I1 a way to fail, the 'neither guard is load-bearing alone' source comment, and methods 3/4. Those belong to the souls piece's round 4.

I did not extend the check to the two FOG-GATE BOSSES. They are not in population-posts.json (they live in hearths.json fog_gates), so the 267 road bodies are the whole of what this cache claims; the 269-body figure the r3 critic quotes adds them separately and no file caches it.

The check counts encounter templates at DEFAULT composition — one template, dres-raid-party, carries an `absent_when_flag` member that a quest can remove. The generator does the same, so the comparison is exact; the caveat is printed under --verbose rather than assumed.
I did not rewrite W1-POPULATION-r1.json, nor any figure inside a stamped verdict body. Annotated instead, and said so above.
No timing figure of any kind is published by this piece, so RULES 26's load-declaration requirement does not bind — but the contention state is declared above anyway.
